_comment: urOMT model/algorithm settings. Data settings (scans, mask, voxel spacing, domain size) are read directly from planC and are NOT stored here. Mirrors cfg fields (b) from the MATLAB getParams.m.

_field_doc.sigma: diffusion coefficient (Gaussian bandwidth) in the advection-diffusion PDE
_field_doc.dt: time-step size for the inner numerical integration
_field_doc.nt: number of inner time sub-steps between two consecutive image frames
_field_doc.beta: weight on the final-image fidelity term (Gamma3)
_field_doc.eta: OPTIONAL weight on a velocity H1-smoothness penalty (Gamma4 = eta*hd*dt*sum|grad u|^2), a pyCERR extension with no counterpart in the reference MATLAB implementation. DEFAULT 0 = off, which keeps the objective identical to the reference. It was briefly defaulted to 1000 to tame an incoherent velocity field, but that incoherence turned out to be a symptom of a non-mass-conserving advection operator (since fixed); with the correct operator, neighbour-vector direction coherence is ~0.88 at eta=0 and rises only to ~0.93 by eta=1000, so the penalty is no longer needed. Enable it only if you deliberately want a smoother (biased) velocity field, e.g. for visualization
_field_doc.niter_pcg: max iterations for the (P)CG Hessian/diffusion solves
_field_doc.maxUiter: outer optimization iterations per time interval (for solver='gn' this is the number of Gauss-Newton steps; few iterations act as early-stopping regularization, as in the MATLAB)
_field_doc.solver: 'gn' = exact Gauss-Newton block (matrix-free GN Hessian 2*beta*hd*J'J + regularization via the final-density sensitivities + CG + backtracking line search; this is the same GN Hessian as MATLAB GNblock_ur); 'lbfgs' = scipy L-BFGS-B on the adjoint gradient (first-pass)
_field_doc.gnLambda0: initial Levenberg-Marquardt damping for solver='gn', relative to the misfit Hessian scale 2*beta*hd; adaptively reduced on accepted steps and raised on rejected ones. DEFAULT 0 = undamped pure Gauss-Newton, matching the reference MATLAB GNblock_ur; raise only for conditioning if a problem will not converge
_field_doc.gnPrecond: 1 = apply a Jacobi preconditioner (from the regularization+damping diagonal) to the Gauss-Newton CG solve. DEFAULT 0 = off, matching the reference implementation's plain pcg. Because diagR carries the factor alpha while diagU does not, the preconditioner is ~alpha stronger on the velocity block, so CG over-steps velocity and starves the source r: with it enabled the solver lands on a ~3.7x worse objective with the source-energy term ~500x too small
_field_doc.gnCgTol: relative residual tolerance for the Gauss-Newton CG solve (MATLAB pcg uses 1e-2)
_field_doc.warm_start: 0 (DEFAULT) = restart every interval from rest (u=0, r=0), matching the reference implementation; 1 = carry the converged (u, r) into the next interval as the starting guess. Warm starting converges further per interval, but because maxUiter is small and acts as early-stopping regularization the velocity ACCUMULATES along the chain: on the reference breast data the kinetic term Gamma1 grew monotonically (4.5e4 -> 3.2e5 across 13 intervals) while the reference stayed flat, and the recovered speed came out several-fold high. The deeper problem is that `maxUiter` is an EARLY-STOPPING regularizer, so warm starting gives later intervals more cumulative optimizer effort than earlier ones - the amount of regularization then varies along the time series. Measured on the reference breast data over 13 intervals: warm_start=1 drove the objective ratio down to 0.41 and the recovered speed to ~4.6x the reference (corr 0.27-0.50); warm_start=0 holds the objective ratio at 0.90-1.14 and speed correlation at 0.86-0.97. This default was changed from 1 to 0 on 2026-08-04
_field_doc.reinitR: 0=initialize each interval with the previous evolved density (consecutive); 1=reset to the measured frame
_field_doc.smooth: total evolution TIME (t_tot) of the smoothing flow applied to each frame (0=off); the number of steps is round(smooth/smooth_dt), matching MATLAB affine_diffusion_3d(A, t_tot, dt, aff). NOTE: this is a time, not a step count
_field_doc.smooth_method: 'affine' (affine-invariant mean-curvature flow, MATLAB affine_diffusion_3d), 'linear' (heat flow), or 'gaussian' (scipy stand-in)
_field_doc.smooth_dt: evolution step size for the affine/linear smoothing flow
_field_doc.convertToConc: 1=concentration ('CC') normalization, 0=raw signal (used only when 'normMethod' is null)
_field_doc.normMethod: signal normalization for Part 1: 'CC' (contrast concentration, needs TR/FA), 'RSE' (relative signal enhancement S(t)/S0), 'none' (raw); null=derive from convertToConc
_field_doc.rhoScale: global rescale of the normalized density (urOMT velocity is scale-invariant, so this only conditions the solver): null/0=off, 'auto'=make the first-frame ROI mean 1 (useful for tiny CC concentrations), or a numeric multiplier
_field_doc.bbox_pad: pad the ROI bounding box outward from the mask's tight box. A SCALAR pads the two in-plane axes only (0=tight box). A 3-element [row, col, slice] pads each axis independently - needed to reproduce the MATLAB getRange, which pads all three (the reference breast run is [3,3,3]: its 61x59x46 grid is the 55x53x40 mask box grown by 3 per side on every axis). Padding never runs off the scan
_field_doc.mask_dilate: grow the ROI mask by this many voxels before it is used to report the Eulerian/Lagrangian maps (the reference implementation's cfg.dilate). Uses the same ellipsoidal structuring element: the voxels of -d:d per axis with (x/d)^2+(y/d)^2+(z/d)^2 <= 1, i.e. a ball of radius d in INDEX space (anisotropic on anisotropic voxels, matching the reference). Applied after the ROI bounding box is fixed, so it widens map coverage without moving the solve domain. 0 = off (pyCERR default); the reference breast run used 2, and reproducing its maps voxel-for-voxel REQUIRES matching it - otherwise pyCERR reports a strictly smaller support
_field_doc.peclet_floor: additive floor on the Peclet denominator |sigma grad log rho|, as a fraction of the ROI-median diffusive speed. Stops voxels in smooth-density regions (denominator -> 0) producing enormous Peclet spikes and a salt-and-pepper map. This is a deliberate departure from the reference, which floors only at machine epsilon, and because the floor is additive it biases Peclet DOWNWARD - most strongly in exactly the high-Peclet voxels. Measured against the reference breast maps, the through-origin slope is 0.67 at the 0.1 default, 0.98 at 0.01 and 1.06 at 0. Use a small value or 0 to reproduce reference Peclet; the default for a display-stable map. NOTE this affects the Eulerian maps only - runGLAD's pathline Peclet always floors at machine epsilon
_field_doc.bbox_full_z: 1=use the full z-extent of the scan for the ROI box instead of the mask's z-range (matches MATLAB getRange)
_field_doc.fft_pad: 1=grow the ROI bounding box on each axis to the next FFT-friendly length (only 2/3/5 as prime factors), staying inside the scan. The implicit-diffusion solve is a 3-D DCT whose cost depends on the prime factorization of the grid dims, not the voxel count: 61x59x46 costs ~15.7 ms per solve vs ~5.9 ms for 64x60x48, which has MORE voxels. Since that solve runs twice per sub-step in every CG matvec, this is ~2.7x on the dominant term. The box only ever grows, so the ROI is never clipped - but it moves the Neumann boundary and therefore changes results slightly. 0=use the tight bounding box
_field_doc.numThreads: number of CPU threads for the solver: the numba trilinear kernels and the thread pool that splits the 3-D DCT diffusion solve. DEFAULT 0 = auto, which is min(cores, 6) and deliberately NOT every core - these kernels are memory-bandwidth bound, so oversubscribing them is measurably SLOWER. Measured on a 24-core box, one CG matvec: 542 ms at 1 thread, 300 ms at 4, 286 ms at 6, 278 ms at 8, 368 ms at 24. Set an explicit number to profile your own machine, or 1 for reproducible single-threaded runs. Results do not depend on the thread count: the kernels are deterministic and the DCT chunking is bit-exact. Values above the process maximum are clamped with a warning - numba fixes that ceiling when it is first imported, so to raise it set the NUMBA_NUM_THREADS environment variable BEFORE importing pyCERR. Accepts the former name 'threads' as an alias
_field_doc.useGPU: 'yes' (or 1) = run the solver on the GPU via cupy (`pip install "pycerr[gpu]"` plus a matching NVIDIA driver; see cerr/uromt/gpu.py for the version rules and a stale-CUDA-toolkit gotcha). DEFAULT 'no' (or 0) = CPU (numba, threaded per numThreads). Falls back to the CPU with a warning if cupy or a device is unavailable. WORTH IT ONLY FOR LARGE ROIs: measured on a Quadro RTX 5000 vs a 24-core CPU at nt=10, the block solve was 3.5x faster at 84k voxels, 6.8x at 184k and 13.2x at 622k - the win grows with ROI size because GPU time stays far flatter than CPU time (small ROIs are partly kernel-launch-latency bound). Results match the CPU to ~1e-9. Not supported with solver=lbfgs
_field_doc.T10: pre-contrast longitudinal relaxation time (seconds) for concentration conversion (default 1/0.6)
_field_doc.basePts: number of leading SELECTED frames consumed in-sequence as the pre-contrast baseline S(0) (only when baselineFrames=0 and the window starts at frame 1)
_field_doc.baselineFrames: external pre-contrast baseline: S(0)=mean of the first N temporally-ordered scans, NOT consumed (the whole selected window is transported). 1=use the 1st timepoint. Matches the MATLAB workflow; >0 overrides the in-sequence basePts consumption
_field_doc.TR: repetition time override in SECONDS; null=read scanInfo.repetitionTime (DICOM milliseconds, converted to seconds automatically)
_field_doc.FA: flip angle (degrees) override for concentration conversion; null=read from scan metadata (scanInfo.flipAngle)
_field_doc.concScale: multiply the concentration by this constant after conversion (the reference tofts recipe uses 150). urOMT velocity is invariant to a global rho scale so this only conditions the solver - but it must match the reference for objective (Gamma) values to be comparable, and it fixes the units that highValueThreshold and outputClip are expressed in, so the three go together. 1.0 = off
_field_doc.highValueThreshold: after concScale, replace voxels above this value by the local mean over a highValueKernel^3 box, to tame isolated spikes (reference: 210). null = disabled. NOTE the reference applies this to the FULL volume before cropping to the ROI while pyCERR applies it after, so voxels within highValueKernel of the ROI face see a slightly different neighbourhood - a handful of voxels on the reference breast data
_field_doc.highValueKernel: edge length in voxels of the box mean used for highValueThreshold (reference: 2, i.e. a 2x2x2 mean)
_field_doc.outputClip: optional [min,max] clip applied to the concentration AFTER concScale and the high-value replacement, before smoothing (reference: [0, 10000]). null = no clip
_field_doc.conc_clip: optional [min,max] clip applied to the normalized signal (S(t)/S(0)) before concentration conversion; null=no clip
_field_doc.chiStructNum: structure index for the source-indicator chi (MATLAB K); null=K=1 everywhere (source r may act anywhere in the ROI)
_field_doc.time: 1-based selection into the supplied scan list: first_time:time_jump:last_time (last_time=null -> last scan)
